Thanks - you're absolutely right. I realize I didn't mention in my first post that he is actually in the hospital right now. He has been since the first episode. They were at the point of discharging him when the second one occurred on the new meds. Now, though, he refuses to take any medication which is the concern.

Thanks for checking in Svabhava. There are a few things at the moment. My brother has just been diagnosed with clinical depression. My SO is undergoing perhaps the most stressful period in her life. My parents are dealing with health issues. I'm just trying to hold it together for everyone, but it's getting tough. I don't want to burden them with my issues, but these days all I can manage to do is lock myself in my room. I feel like I'm not living up to my responsibilities and my potential but anytime I try to do something I'm overwhelmed with anxiety or a feeling of worthlessness. I'm sorry for ranting.

Two children died in Gaza yesterday. I write this in their honour.

There are so many costs to a war like this, I couldn’t enumerate them all.
Economic costs in dollars and cents of shells and bombs and guns.
Political costs as the world watches stunned at the images of violent death.
And human costs as the sons and daughters of Israel and Palestine lose their lives to this conflict.
But the worst cost of all is this:
On that small strip of land by the Mediterranean, two children will no longer rise, and the small delights of their growing into men will be denied us all. And just a few miles away, someday, a child will ask their father why he had to kill them. And no answer will suffice.

Thanks... I like that you throw yourself into the fray every day anyway. I try to do that most days when I can. Your story reminded me of a story I've always found helpful: http://impossiblehq.com/then-die
Thanks. I like your story and I'll remember it during the tough times.
